scope: Proposition 5.9 (Core block projections) of the manuscript “Donovan's Conjecture over Algebraically Closed Fields” (preprints/Donovans-Conjecture-over-Algebraic-Closures-of-Prime-Fields-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 203 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 80d721e72d29a9bc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In each remaining type-A unipotent target, and in each regular classical target with fixed p′-parameter s, the following holds. Partition the basic rows in E(HF, s) by their packed core collections, using the actual unordered-symbol and type-D identifications. Each part is the intersection of that basic set with a union of blocks in Ep(HF, s). Distinct core collections cannot occur in the same block. Split sign choices within one underlying core may be merged. This remains true in every intermediate split Levi with the specified frozen extractions, and after the common central p-quotient. Consequently all these core projections are projections by sums of block idempotents on projective modules.
